daily_brief: The day's news is dominated by civil unrest spreading across Europe, with France implementing targeted curfews in Paris, Lyon, and other cities after a weekend of violent protests over rising fuel prices and deteriorating public services left thousands of businesses damaged and more than 120 people imprisoned [BBC, RFI, Globe and Mail]. Le Monde reports similar unrest in Italy, Spain, Belgium, and Portugal amid soaring energy prices and housing crises. In Ukraine, President Zelensky's adviser told the BBC that Ukrainians have died due to US restrictions on intelligence sharing, contradicting White House denials of any changes [BBC, France 24, Globe and Mail]. Canada received welcome news as Alberta voters decisively rejected a referendum on independence by 76% to 23%, a significant victory for Prime Minister Mark Carney amid ongoing tensions with the Trump administration [Financial Times, RFI, ABC Australia, Al Jazeera]. In Sudan, a drone strike near a market killed 80 people in one of the deadliest single attacks since the civil war began in 2023 [The Guardian]. Meanwhile, a Kenyan court found cult leader Paul Mackenzie guilty of murdering 191 people, mostly children, in what became known as the Shakahola Forest Massacre [The Guardian, France 24, RFI].

top_stories.headline: France Imposes Targeted Curfews After Weekend of Violent Protests Over Cost of Living
bullets: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu instructed regional authorities to impose partial curfews in Paris, Lyon, Nice, Lille, and other cities after protests over fuel prices, cost of living, and education deteriorated into rioting and looting
More than 120 people have been imprisoned and approximately 3,000 businesses across France were damaged or looted over the weekend; the historic 19th-century Limoges city hall was gutted by fire
A 40-year-old suspect linked to far-left movements and classified as a national security threat was arrested in connection with the Limoges fire
Government officials stated they have not ruled out a state of emergency but emphasized curfews are preferable to measures that would restrict freedoms for all citizens

top_stories.headline: Zelensky Adviser Says Ukrainians Dying Due to US Intelligence Restrictions; White House Denies Changes
bullets: Senior Zelensky adviser Serhii Beskrestnov told the BBC that Ukrainian lives have been lost because Kyiv is not receiving reliable US warnings of incoming Russian ballistic missile attacks
Zelensky reported two overnight ballistic missile attacks on Kyiv, one without warning and another with minimal time to shelter; restrictions on Ukraine's use of Starlink remain in place
The White House denied any changes to intelligence sharing; Ukraine first reported interruptions last week amid disputes over a US deal to import Russian diesel from Moscow
Trump envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are expected to travel to Norway for fresh talks with Zelensky as US midterm elections approach

top_stories.headline: Alberta Voters Decisively Reject Independence Referendum, Handing Victory to Canadian Unity
bullets: Approximately 76% of Alberta voters rejected a proposal to begin a process toward independence, with 23% supporting the measure, in results projected by CBC and CTV
Prime Minister Mark Carney called it a 'clear choice' for unity amid ongoing US trade war and annexation threats from President Trump
The referendum was non-binding and would not have directly separated Alberta from Canada, but would have initiated a legal process toward a future binding vote
Separatist leaders, including Jeffrey Rath of the Alberta Prosperity Project, said they will continue pursuing independence despite the defeat

top_stories.headline: Drone Strike Near Sudan Market Kills 80 in One of War's Deadliest Single Attacks
bullets: A drone struck twice near a market in al-Dibab, West Kordofan state, killing 80 people, mostly commuters waiting for transport home after market day
The attack hit a transport hub 10 minutes apart; 50 bodies were buried locally while 30 of 47 transported to nearby al-Mujlad died from injuries
The RSF-aligned administration accused the Sudanese armed forces of carrying out the strike; the area is under RSF control
Between January and April 2026, drone strikes accounted for at least 880 civilian deaths, representing over 80% of all conflict-related civilian casualties

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.framing_note: Provided detailed witness accounts and broader context on drone warfare escalation in the conflict

top_stories.headline: Kenyan Cult Leader Found Guilty of Murdering 191 People in Shakahola Forest Starvation Deaths
bullets: Paul Mackenzie and 28 associates were found guilty of murdering 190 children and one adult by ordering followers to starve themselves and their children to death to 'meet Jesus'
More than 400 bodies have been recovered from shallow graves in Shakahola forest since 2023; only 26 have been identified due to severe decomposition
The judge stated that in some cases children were isolated and denied food while their parents watched; Mackenzie denied forcing victims to starve
Mackenzie also faces separate charges of manslaughter and terrorism; the case represents one of the worst cult-related disasters in recent history

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.framing_note: Emphasized scale of tragedy and provided family victim perspectives

sources.framing_note: Included calls for tougher regulation of religious organizations
